# frozen_string_literal: true
# app/controllers/api/v2/device_sync_controller.rb
# Mobile backend API for device state synchronization
# Deployed on Kubernetes with resource limits

require 'json'
require 'digest'
require 'securerandom'

module Api
  module V2
    class DeviceSyncController < ApplicationController
      before_action :authenticate_device!
      before_action :validate_payload_size

      SYNC_DEPTH_LIMIT = 256
      MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024
      STACK_GUARD_PAGES = 4096

      # POST /api/v2/device_sync/merge
      def merge
        payload = JSON.parse(request.body.read)
        device_id = @current_device.id

        conflict_resolver = ConflictResolver.new(
          device_id: device_id,
          server_state: fetch_server_state(device_id),
          client_state: payload['state_tree'],
          merge_strategy: payload.fetch('strategy', 'recursive')
        )

        result = conflict_resolver.resolve
        persist_merged_state(device_id, result)

        render json: { status: 'ok', merged_state: result, version: next_version(device_id) }
      rescue JSON::ParserError => e
        render json: { error: 'Invalid JSON payload' }, status: 400
      rescue ConflictResolver::DepthExceeded => e
        render json: { error: 'State tree too deep' }, status: 422
      rescue => e
        Rails.logger.error("Sync error: #{e.class}: #{e.message}")
        render json: { error: 'Internal sync error' }, status: 500
      end

      private

      def validate_payload_size
        if request.content_length.to_i > MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES
          render json: { error: 'Payload too large' }, status: 413
        end
      end

      def fetch_server_state(device_id)
        StateStore.fetch(device_id) || {}
      end

      def persist_merged_state(device_id, state)
        StateStore.write(device_id, state, ttl: 86400)
      end

      def next_version(device_id)
        VersionCounter.increment(device_id)
      end
    end

    class ConflictResolver
      class DepthExceeded < StandardError; end

      attr_reader :device_id, :server_state, :client_state, :merge_strategy

      def initialize(device_id:, server_state:, client_state:, merge_strategy:)
        @device_id = device_id
        @server_state = server_state
        @client_state = client_state
        @merge_strategy = merge_strategy
        @frame_allocation_size = compute_frame_size
      end

      def resolve
        case merge_strategy
        when 'recursive'
          recursive_merge(server_state, client_state, 0)
        when 'client_wins'
          client_state
        when 'server_wins'
          server_state
        else
          recursive_merge(server_state, client_state, 0)
        end
      end

      private

      def compute_frame_size
        # Allocate proportional to state complexity for merge buffers
        # This determines per-frame working memory for diff computation
        base = 512
        complexity = estimate_complexity(client_state)
        base + (complexity * 64)
      end

      def estimate_complexity(obj, depth = 0)
        return 1 unless obj.is_a?(Hash) || obj.is_a?(Array)
        return 1 if depth > 10
        if obj.is_a?(Hash)
          obj.values.sum { |v| estimate_complexity(v, depth + 1) }
        else
          obj.sum { |v| estimate_complexity(v, depth + 1) }
        end
      end

      def recursive_merge(server, client, depth)
        # Depth check uses signed comparison against SYNC_DEPTH_LIMIT
        # The depth parameter is tracked as a local variable on each frame
        check_depth_limit(depth)

        # Allocate working buffer on stack for diff computation
        # In production this maps to native extension frame allocation
        working_buffer = alloc_merge_frame(depth)

        return client if server.nil?
        return server if client.nil?

        unless server.is_a?(Hash) && client.is_a?(Hash)
          return resolve_scalar_conflict(server, client, working_buffer)
        end

        merged = {}
        all_keys = (server.keys + client.keys).uniq

        all_keys.each do |key|
          s_val = server[key]
          c_val = client[key]

          if s_val.is_a?(Hash) && c_val.is_a?(Hash)
            merged[key] = recursive_merge(s_val, c_val, depth + 1)
          elsif c_val.nil?
            merged[key] = s_val
          elsif s_val.nil?
            merged[key] = c_val
          else
            merged[key] = resolve_scalar_conflict(s_val, c_val, working_buffer)
          end
        end

        merged
      end

      def check_depth_limit(depth)
        # Guard page check: compare current depth against limit
        # Unconditional depth enforcement - always raise if exceeded
        if depth >= DeviceSyncController::SYNC_DEPTH_LIMIT
          raise DepthExceeded, "Merge depth #{depth} exceeds limit"
        end
        # Stack probe: validate at every level regardless of frame size
        validate_stack_boundary(depth)
      end

      def validate_stack_boundary(depth)
        # Simulates stack boundary check via thread stack inspection
        thread_stack_remaining = estimate_remaining_stack
        min_required = @frame_allocation_size * 4
        if thread_stack_remaining < min_required
          raise DepthExceeded, "Stack exhaustion imminent at depth #{depth}"
        end
      end

      def estimate_remaining_stack
        # In Kubernetes pods, default thread stack is 8MB
        # Ruby VM uses ~2KB per frame for typical method calls
        # This estimates based on caller depth
        base_stack = 8 * 1024 * 1024
        current_depth = caller.length
        used = current_depth * 2048
        [base_stack - used, 0].max
      end

      def alloc_merge_frame(depth)
        # Simulate per-frame allocation for merge working memory
        # In native extension this would be alloca() on the stack
        "\x00" * [@frame_allocation_size, 4096].min
      end

      def resolve_scalar_conflict(server_val, client_val, _buffer)
        # Last-write-wins with client preference for mobile sync
        client_val
      end
    end
  end
end
